scope: Official documentation verification only; no host compatibility, permissions, performance or operational validation

sources.claim: Rollback-journal atomic commit relies on filesystem, locking and flush assumptions; documentation is not proof of this host's power-loss durability.
EXTRA adds directory synchronization after rollback-journal deletion; SQLite recommends EXTRA when rollback-mode durability is required.
BEGIN IMMEDIATE starts a write transaction immediately and may return SQLITE_BUSY if another writer is active.
WAL uses additional files and coordination; official documentation reports a WAL-reset race fixed in3.51.3 and specified backports. No installed SQLite version was checked.
The online backup API creates database backups through SQLite; it is a candidate for coherent archival snapshots, not proof against application-level rollback/replay.
A pipe security descriptor controls access; default permissions include read access for Everyone and anonymous. Explicit narrowly scoped access is necessary for the proposed profile.
PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS rejects remote connections. The documentation distinguishes overlapped I/O from PIPE_NOWAIT, which is not the recommended asynchronous mechanism.
Python supplies keyed HMAC and recommends compare_digest for externally supplied authentication tags to reduce timing exposure. HMAC is not asymmetric non-repudiation.
RFC8785 is an Informational JSON canonicalization specification; it rejects duplicate properties and recommends strings for numbers needing precision beyond IEEE754 double representation.
DPAPI protection is normally tied to the same logon credentials and computer. This does not protect against compromise of the authorized principal or supply portable institutional key escrow.
Process query, synchronization and termination are distinct access rights. Minimal observation rights do not imply authority to terminate a process.
Jobs manage groups of processes; assignment, inherited jobs and nesting affect scope. Group containment is not proof that this host permits a safe owned-only fallback.
monotonic_ns returns integer nanoseconds without float precision loss. Its reference is not UTC; sleep scheduling can overshoot a requested duration, so this is not a real-time guarantee.
The API retrieves a named pipe client's process ID; that value still needs creation/generation/ownership verification.
The API retrieves a named pipe server's process ID; that alone is not trusted ownership proof.
GetProcessTimes returns process creation/exit timing through a process handle with required query rights; no such host call was performed here.
